task_instance: Take a realistic weak prompt ('Summarize this support ticket and tell me what to do.') and produce an optimized, production-ready prompt by applying the skill's prompt-engineering method: diagnose the weak-prompt problems, rewrite using the RSCIT framework, add the structured-JSON-output and reduce-hallucination patterns and length constraints, then verify against the skill's Prompt Audit Checklist.
evidence: This skill is a self-contained prompt-engineering methodology (no bundled scripts, SDK or model call required; its own Limitations section says to apply judgment, not run a program). Created sample input weak_prompt.txt. Produced optimized_prompt.md containing: (1) a diagnosis mapping the weak prompt to the skill's problem/symptom/fix table; (2) a rewritten prompt with all five RSCIT elements (Role, Situation, Constraints, Instructions, Template); (3) the skill's structured-JSON-output pattern with an enumerated schema; (4) the reduce-hallucination grounding clause and no-guess/null rule; (5) explicit length constraints and section delimiters; (6) a completed 6-item Prompt Audit Checklist. Verified with a python3 -I script (no model, no network): confirmed all 5 RSCIT markers present, all 6 applied skill patterns present (grounding, no-guess rule, 'VALID JSON ONLY', 40-word length cap, '---' delimiters, enumerated P1/P2/P3), all 6 audit checkboxes ticked, and that a schema-conformant sample model response parses as valid JSON with all required keys and valid enum values. Files: weak_prompt.txt, optimized_prompt.md, verification run output. No model calls were made (not needed for this methodology skill), so the CLAUDE.md URL-guard/sandbox model rules were not engaged; no credentials, network services, or MCP/connector tools were used; all work stayed inside the work directory.
